title: Group splitting (split-and-rebuild): transactional split of a task group into two closed-form specialists + fused readout, vs the incumbent and a random-split control
question: When a registered task group contains two subpopulations, can the registry split it into two closed-form specialists plus a fused readout without losing accuracy - and is the win real structure rather than an artefact of the proposal step?

registration_notes.N98.1: Input: the M143 cached score matrices (v16/m143/scores.npz), never recomputed. A group = the test rows of one domain (the incumbent specialist's group). The whole experiment runs on held-out rows, exactly like M143's stacking protocol.
registration_notes.N98.2: Per group: rows split 50/50 (fit/eval, seeded per domain). Fit half: incumbent ridge on all fit rows; proposal = seeded 2-means over the standardised 2415-dim score vectors -> children X, Y; child ridges on their cluster rows; fusion = stacking over [X_scores, Y_scores] with the penalty ladder selected on a validation slice of the fit half.
registration_notes.N98.3: Controls: a seeded RANDOM split runs the identical recipe; the split signal must beat it. Row floor: groups with fewer than 2 x floor fit rows or a degenerate cluster are SKIPPED, not failed (data starvation, E10).
registration_notes.N98.4: Gate (kill switch): a domain PASSES iff fused(2-means) >= incumbent + margin AND fused(2-means) >= fused(random) on its eval half. M149 fires iff ZERO domains pass (the split operation has no measured room on these groups - a scoped negative); otherwise PASS with the per-domain table.
registration_notes.N98.5: Smoke runs declare _smoke_note and MUST refuse the sealed output directory.
registration_notes.N98.6: Dated snapshot; all seeds, the ladder, the floor and the margin registered for byte-repeat.

gate.registered: domain passes iff fused(2-means) >= incumbent + 0.005 AND fused(2-means) >= fused(random) on its eval half; fired iff ZERO domains pass.
gate.consequence_fired: the split operation has no measured room on these groups; M149 closes as a scoped negative and splitting stays registered but unproven on this corpus.
gate.consequence_passed: split-and-rebuild beats the incumbent on at least one domain and beats the random-split control: the registry split is a measured operation, promotable with its transactional gates.
